items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: I want to be loud and © Fillius Jazz Archive -12- brass, Maynard Ferguson style.

ctx.x: Over the years I’ve had, especially in middle school-aged, promising musicians but they were really shy. And I saw you speak in an interview and you described yourself as a quiet person. And I used to say to these shy young musicians, “Think of your instrument like a prop, like when an actor gets a cane and a hat they’re transforming themselves.” And I wonder if you ever thought about your trumpet as a prop that allows me to step outside of my regular personality?

Yeah I think the trumpet has that ability more so than other instruments. You know I taught in the public schools for about 12, 13 years and I taught woodwind and brass. I taught clarinet, you know, tenor, alto, trombone, I had some trumpet students. And yeah it’s like the trumpet has a certain magnetism that attracts certain types of people, you know really loud outspoken people or maybe really reserved people that want to have something that’s on the opposite end of what they are. And then you have some that…

brass, Maynard Ferguson style. And then you have other people, it’s like I really want to make this brass instrument that wants to be loud and high be something that’s more subtle like Chet Baker or, you know somebody else. So yeah for me it’s probably a mix of that. But I say I’ve really gotten a little bit out of my — I mean I’ve gotten older and, you know, developed more as a person and so I’ve kind of come out of my shell that way but I think just being on the educational side of things really opened me up…
